character:
Character sheet for 2D animation rigging: the Cheshire Cat, of Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), as John Tenniel drew him. Copy ONLY the LAYOUT of the FIRST attached sheet (what goes where): take NOTHING of its character. No man, no armour, no hair, no human hands. Take the STYLE from the SECOND attached image.

The Cheshire Cat: a LARGE, solid, round-faced tabby cat, as big as a man sitting at a table; a warm grey-brown coat with darker brown tabby stripes, a cream chin and chest; round yellow-green eyes, pointed ears, long white whiskers; and an ENORMOUS grin stretching from ear to ear, full of neat white teeth: the grin is the most important thing about him and must read at a tiny size. A long, thick striped tail. He sits up at the table like a person, on his haunches, his two front paws resting on the table's edge. Lazy, amused, mischievous, completely unbothered. HIS FUR: a bold dark outline; the fur shown by a few chunky tufts on the outline at the cheeks, the ruff of his chest and the ears, with soft strokes inside them in the shadows only, never hair by hair. Warm grey-brown with a few broad, darker tabby bands following the body, a cream chin and chest, with the warm lamplit rim light along his ears, shoulders and tail. Big round yellow-green eyes with a slit pupil and one highlight; three plain whisker lines a side; the teeth one clean white band with a few lines. A big, sly, grown-up cat with a little menace in the grin, never cute, never a cuddly toy. NOT the Disney cat: NO pink, NO purple, NO bright stripes. Nothing from any film.

Pure white background (#FFFFFF). Every piece separate, with a closed dark outline and a wide gap all round it; nothing touches or overlaps. No text, no labels, no frames, no cast shadows.

The angle: a gentle three-quarter view, turned about 25 degrees from front-on, facing the viewer's right. Both eyes, the whole grin and both shoulders clearly visible. NOT profile.

Draw, all facing the viewer's right, at the same size:
- Finished heads, each with the ears, whiskers, neck and the top of the chest: grinning, calm; talking, mouth open mid-word inside the grin; one eye shut, the other open; eyes narrowed to slits, the grin thinner
- The grin on its own, floating, with nothing else: just the lips, the teeth and the dark mouth line, as it looks when the rest of the cat has vanished
- The body: chest and shoulders sitting upright, NO head (cut off just below the chin), cut off straight below the chest; NO front legs
- Two front legs and paws, lying on a table, pointing toward its centre, open at the shoulder end
- The long striped tail on its own, curled up in a loose S
- Four seated reference poses, sitting up behind the curved edge of a round green poker table, both front paws resting on its edge, apart, his tail curled up beside him on the left of the picture: grinning, calm; his tail and back half vanished (simply not drawn, plain white), only his front half left; one eye shut; the tip of his tail twitching

style: STYLE, the most important rule: match the SECOND attached image (the Headless Horseman, from the Transylvania table) exactly: a GOTHIC GRAPHIC-NOVEL style for a grown-up card game, halfway between a bright cartoon and a dark painted illustration. Take NOTHING of his character: no armour, no pumpkin, no cloak, no man: ONE head, a CAT. Keep what the game needs: a bold dark outline round every shape, big clear readable shapes, a silhouette that reads at a tiny size. Adult, realistic proportions (never a big head, never chibi, never cute); shading in three or four tones with deep, dramatic shadows and a warm rim light from candlelight; rich but MUTED colour, nothing candy-bright; cloth with real weight and heavy folds; a little texture in the shadows only. Serious, weary and a little dangerous. NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute, NOT toy-like, NOT round and bouncy, NOT photoreal, NOT muddy or murky.
style_short: Keep the gothic graphic-novel style of the attached sheets and of the Headless Horseman's sheet: bold dark outlines, adult proportions, deep three- or four-tone shading, a warm lamplit rim light, rich muted colour; serious and sombre, NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute.
